sections.title: Thanks before asking
sections.line: Paul prays because of a report, not a problem.

sections.title: A prayer for sight
sections.line: He asks for eyes to see what they already have.

sections.title: Power with a measure
sections.line: Resurrection and enthronement set the yardstick for power in believers.

sections.title: Given to the church
sections.line: Universal rule handed over specifically for the church's sake.

themes.note: The prayer is for perception, not for more provision.
Strength in believers is measured by the empty tomb.
Every competing authority is named, then placed underneath.
Cosmic rule is given to him on the church's behalf.

references.why: Humanity's mandate over creation is claimed for Christ, so the church's head already rules everything under his feet.
Echoes Nebuchadnezzar's boast of mighty power, relocating an imperial king's language onto God's work in the resurrection.
Supplies the name above every name that Paul assumes here when he writes 'every name that is named'.
Same list of rule, authority and power — but there Paul dates their abolition, not just their subjection.
The sister letter's version of head over the body, showing this is Paul's settled way of joining rule to church.

purpose: Paul wants us to know the power at work in believers is the same power that raised Christ, so that we stop measuring it by our own strength.
He prays for enlightened eyes rather than new gifts, because what the Ephesians lack is not provision but sight of what they already hold.
He wants us to believe Christ's universal rule was given for the church, so that cosmic authority reads as personal care, not distant power.
